title: The Nature of Skepticism in Epistemology
text:
Epistemological skepticism questions the limits and reliability of human knowledge, challenging foundational assumptions about how truth is ascertained. It explores whether absolute certainty regarding external reality or knowledge acquisition is actually achievable.

Historically, skepticism has led to deep examinations of sensory experience and rational deduction, prompting schools of thought like Pyrrhonism and Cartesian doubt. The modern discussion often involves distinguishing between methodological skepticism (doubt used as a tool for discovery) and inherent, radical skepticism (the belief that certainty is impossible).

Ultimately, the dialogue surrounding skepticism rarely mandates an absolute conclusion, but rather establishes the necessary criteria and parameters by which claims to knowledge must be evaluated.
